To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

endothelial cells on a compliant substrate will self-assemble into a network-like structure through the proliferation and migration, that these networks form through the propagation of traction force generated strains from the cell edges, and that the formation of these networks is transient, with cell migration from the network edges filling in the gaps between cells as the network matures.
substrate elasticity influences the formation of endothelial cell networks and the traction forces generated by endothelial cells on the substrate.

(1) endothelial cells self- assemble into networks on compliant substrates, (2) these cell-cell interactions are mediated by fibronectin, and (3) cell traction force may direct endothelial cell assembly and network formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how endothelial cells sense and respond to the mechanical cues in their environment, and how this information is integrated into cell-cell interactions and collective behavior.
the role of mechanical forces in the assembly of endothelial cells into networks, and how these networks may be used to study the formation of blood vessels.
the effects of substrate elasticity, endothelium cell-cell connectivity and cellular traction forces on angiogenesis and vasulogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
substrate elasticity is a key determinant in endothelial network formation.
the mechanical properties of a substrate can affect the assembly of endothelial cells into network-like structures.
the substrate mechanics and cell traction force play important roles in endothelial network formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical microenvironment can influence endothelial cell assembly and network formation.
endothelial cell network self-assembly and formation is dependent on substrate mechanics, and that traction force generation is a driving force for cell migration, and therefore cell-cell assembly.
substrate elasticity can influence endothelial cell network assembly and that the traction forces generated by the cells can promote this assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mechanical environment can have a significant impact on the assembly of endothelial cells and that the mechanical environment may have a more significant impact on endothelial cell assembly than previously appreciated.
substrate mechanics can influence cell-cell interactions and that this influence may be a key component in the assembly of endothelial cell networks.
substrate elasticity and cellular traction force may play an important role in endothelial network formation and vasculogenesis.
